content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"All three consensus responses identify righteousness primarily as right standing before God together with conformity to His character and standard — in salvation contexts a status granted by grace through faith apart from works, classically pictured as imputed/credited righteousness (Gen 15:6; Rom 3-4; Phil 3:9; 2 Cor 5:21). Ethical conduct, transformative/infused righteousness, covenant faithfulness, God's own saving justice, and social justice are listed as recognized alternatives, with the mechanism (imputed vs. infused vs. covenantal) acknowledged as confessionally contested.","book_summary":"The book defines righteousness as 'right-living': God is Right-Living by definition and His ways are the measure of right; for those under His authority, righteousness is the doing of His commandments — the law kept, worn as the garment of righteous acts. It reinterprets Romans 4 as excluding only wage-work that would put God in debt, not obedience (via Luke 17:7-10's unprofitable servant), affirms that righteousness is given and reckoned by grace, but insists the gift never renames wrong-living right.","consensus_core_identification":"Righteousness = right standing/relationship with God plus conformity to His moral standard, received in salvation contexts as a gracious gift through faith apart from works (dominantly framed as imputed forensic status).","book_core_identification":"Righteousness = right-living, i.e., actual doing of God's commandments measured by God's own character; reckoned by grace, but constitutively conduct-conformity — never a status label detached from or contrary to actual right-living.","core_relation":"BOOK_NARROWS","extension_relation":"PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION","boundary_disagreement":"The book reclassifies the 'works' excluded in Romans 4: consensus reads 'apart from works' as excluding obedience-based righteousness generally (righteousness credited apart from law-keeping), while the book restricts the exclusion to wage-work that would obligate God, keeping commandment-obedience inside the definition of righteousness itself. Correspondingly, the book excludes cases the dominant consensus reading admits: a person reckoned righteous while still 'wrong-living' (imputed status renaming the ungodly). Consensus treats right-living as fruit/evidence of righteousness; the book treats it as the referent.","material_contradiction":"The book's claim that 'the gift never renames wrong-living right' and that Romans 4 does not exclude obedience contradicts the dominant Protestant imputation reading (Rom 4:5, God 'justifieth the ungodly'; righteousness 'without works'), which all three responses present as the primary or dominant mechanism. However, this contradicts the leading mechanism-alternative, not the broad shared category of 'rightness according to God,' and the book's position substantially overlaps the consensus-listed transformative/ethical alternatives (1 John 3:7; Matt 5:20 readings).","rationale":"Both readings operate within the same category: rightness defined by God's character and standard. The consensus responses themselves include conformity to God's will and ethical conduct within or alongside the core, and list transformative/conduct-based righteousness as a common alternative. The book does not replace the referent with something unrecognizable; it elevates the conduct-conformity strand to the definition, retains 'given and reckoned by grace,' and materially redraws the boundary of Romans 4's excluded 'works.' That is a real boundary disagreement — rejecting status-apart-from-conduct cases and admitting obedience into the definition — but not a replacement of the central referent. Hence REFINED with BOOK_NARROWS at the core and PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION at the extension.","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"One could argue DIVERGENT: the consensus's minimum core is 'right standing before God received by faith apart from works,' and the book's core is 'right-living by commandment-keeping,' with an explicit denial that the gift renames wrong-living right — a direct contradiction of the imputed-status-to-the-ungodly identification that all three responses make primary. If the forensic status is treated as the consensus's central referent rather than one mechanism within a broader category, the book replaces it. The REFINED verdict depends on reading the consensus core broadly (standing + conformity), which the responses' own wording supports but does not compel. Additionally, the printed excerpts (Rom 4:5-6 'worketh not... without works') sit uneasily with the book's wage-work-only reading, weakening the entry's standalone support.","confidence":"medium"}
